sources.title: Carroll v. United States, 267 U.S. 132 (1925)
sources.author: Taft, C.J. (Opinion of the Court)
sources.organization: Supreme Court of the United States
relevant_locations: Opinion of the Court (Taft, C.J.), holding + mobility rationale
sources.quotation_note: Quotable: distinction between search of a structure vs a vehicle 'because the vehicle can be quickly moved out of the locality or jurisdiction in which the warrant must be sought.'
sources.notes: Origin of the automobile exception. Facts: 68 bottles of whisky/gin behind the upholstery; Prohibition. Author Taft; McReynolds (w/ Sutherland) dissented; reported 6-2 (numeric tally 'as reported', not opinion-verbatim).

sources.title: Collins v. Virginia, 584 U.S. ___ (2018) (No. 16-1027)
sources.author: Sotomayor, J. (Opinion of the Court)
sources.organization: Supreme Court of the United States
relevant_locations: Opinion of the Court (Sotomayor, J.), holding on curtilage
sources.quotation_note: Quotable: 'The scope of the automobile exception extends no further than the automobile itself.'
sources.rights_note: Public domain (federal judicial opinion). Official PDF: https://www.supremecourt.gov/opinions/17pdf/16-1027_7lio.pdf
sources.notes: Anchor case. 8-1; Sotomayor majority; Thomas concurrence (in judgment/opinion); Alito lone dissent. Officer David Rhodes; Ryan Collins; motorcycle under a tarp in the driveway (curtilage).

sources.title: Arizona v. Gant, 556 U.S. 332 (2009)
sources.author: Stevens, J. (Opinion of the Court)
sources.organization: Supreme Court of the United States
relevant_locations: Holding on search incident to arrest of a vehicle
sources.quotation_note: Two-part rule: unsecured + reaching distance, OR reason to believe evidence of the offense of arrest is in the car.
sources.notes: 5-4, Stevens. Separate from the automobile exception (limits SITA in cars).

sources.title: Byrd v. United States, 584 U.S. ___ (2018) (No. 16-1371)
sources.author: Kennedy, J. (Opinion of the Court)
sources.organization: Supreme Court of the United States
sources.quotation_note: A driver in lawful possession/control of a rental car generally has a reasonable expectation of privacy even if not on the rental agreement.
sources.notes: Unanimous 9-0, Kennedy. Remanded on two open issues.

sources.title: United States v. Ross, 456 U.S. 798 (1982)
sources.author: Stevens, J. (Opinion of the Court)
sources.organization: Supreme Court of the United States
relevant_locations: Scope of a warrantless automobile search
sources.quotation_note: Scope 'is defined by the object of the search and the places in which there is probable cause to believe that it may be found.'
sources.notes: 6-3, Stevens. Scope reaches containers where the object could be.

sources.title: California v. Acevedo, 500 U.S. 565 (1991)
sources.author: Blackmun, J. (Opinion of the Court)
sources.organization: Supreme Court of the United States
sources.quotation_note: Police may search a closed container in a car without a warrant on probable cause it holds contraband/evidence.

sources.title: Pennsylvania v. Labron, 518 U.S. 938 (1996)
sources.author: Per Curiam
sources.organization: Supreme Court of the United States
relevant_locations: No separate exigency beyond ready mobility
sources.quotation_note: 'If a car is readily mobile and probable cause exists to believe it contains contraband, the Fourth Amendment ... permits police to search the vehicle without more.'
sources.notes: Reaffirmed by Maryland v. Dyson, 527 U.S. 465 (1999) (docket URL https://www.law.cornell.edu/supremecourt/text/98-1062): 'no separate exigency requirement.'
